ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a full-bridge/H-bridge converter powered by a 220 V DC power supply. The power supply on the left is labeled 220 V, with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative. There are four switches in the bridge arms: the upper left is S1, the lower left is S4, the upper right is S3, and the lower right is S2. The load LOAD is connected between the midpoints of the left and right bridge arms, and the reference polarity of the output voltage vo(t) is marked with the left end positive and the right end negative. Reasoning: When diagonal switches S1 and S2 are on, the left end of the load is connected to the positive DC terminal and the right end is connected to the negative DC terminal, so vo = +220 V. When the other diagonal switches S3 and S4 are on, the right end of the load is connected to the positive DC terminal and the left end is connected to the negative DC terminal, so vo = -220 V. The problem states that vo(t) is controlled as a 400 Hz square wave, so it can be regarded as a symmetrical bipolar square wave with an amplitude of 220 V. The fundamental peak value of a symmetrical bipolar square wave is 4V/pi, so the fundamental RMS value is (4*220/pi)/sqrt(2) = 4*220/(pi*sqrt(2)) ≈ 198.1 V. Rounded to volts, it is 198 V.
